title: docs(detail-view): teach `dueLike` where a detail-view field is authored
body:
Fixes #10057

PR objectui#9993 declared `dueLike?: boolean` on the published `DetailViewField`
twin. The repository taught that key **only on object field metadata**, so an
author could not learn from the docs that it is authorable on a detail-view
field entry — the surface that PR opened. `AGENTS.md` commandment **#2** is the
rule this card was filed under.

## The reading, re-taken on this branch's base

⛔ Not copied from the card. Every zero carries a same-subject control lit by the
**same command**.

**BEFORE** — base `0c2eb5eee`:

```
$ grep -no -E 'dueLike|DetailViewField' content/docs/api/schema-reference.md ; echo "exit=$?"
1150:DetailViewField
exit=0
```
Subject `dueLike`: no hit on the page where a `detail-view` node and its `fields`
entries are authored. Control `DetailViewField`: lit, in that same command.

```
$ grep -rno -E 'dueLike|DateTimeFieldMetadata' content/ ; echo "exit=$?"
```
`dueLike` resolved to `content/docs/fields/date.mdx` and
`content/docs/fields/datetime.mdx` and nowhere else in the tree; the control
`DateTimeFieldMetadata` lit in both of those files in the same command.

**AFTER** — `1974a74ac`, the same two commands: `dueLike` now resolves in
`content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` as well, controls still lit.

**One correction to the card.** The card says the two field pages mention no
detail view, which holds. It does not say where `DetailViewField` *is*
documented: the `DetailViewSchema` section of `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`
names it in the `fields` row of its property table, and teaches none of the
field entry's own keys. That section is where this change lands.

## What changed

**`content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` — the `DetailViewSchema` section.** A
note beside the existing retirement note: what the key marks, a `fields` entry
that shows it, the fact that only a declared `true` short-circuits, and the
precedence between an authored entry and the object's own field metadata. The
example field is named `end_date` on purpose — a neutral name, so the key is
load-bearing rather than shadowed by the due/deadline field-name convention.

**The runtime rule is ⛔ not restated there.** It has one home already: the
DateTime field page's "Overdue Affordance" section, which the Date field page
already cites. The new note cites it too. That section gains the two facts it
was missing, so the citation is honest:

- the red styling and the "Overdue Nd" wording do not switch on and off
  together — red starts the day after the deadline, the wording a day later
  still, and the wording stops when the relative face falls back to an absolute
  date while the red does not;
- `dueLike: false` does not suppress the field-name fallback (the sentence that
  stated this rule was garbled, and it is the very rule the card names).

## Evidence

Every exit code captured **before** any pipe; every gate re-run as the last act
before pushing, on the committed tree `1974a74ac` with `git status` clean.

| Gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-example-ids.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` + the two edited paths | 0 |

`check:doc-snippets` first answered `PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2)` — not a
verdict. Its scoped build ran through the shared verify lock
(`VERDICT command-exit 0`) and the gate then judged every covered block and
passed. No changeset is owed: the presence gate's own verdict line says no
published source or contract of a released package moved. Not a governed
surface, per the guard's own `--test` verdict.

**The behaviour was measured, not copied.** A throw-away rendering probe drew a
`date` detail-view field through `DetailSection` at day offsets, then was
deleted (`git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean afterwards) — 5/5 legs:

- 1 day past, neutral name, `dueLike: true` → red on, "Overdue" **absent**;
- 2 days past → red **and** the wording;
- 30 days past → red still on, wording gone (absolute fallback) — red outlives it;
- `dueLike: false` on a due-named field → both halves still on, so `false` is no opt-out;
- CONTROL, neutral name and no key → asserted **by value** ("days ago" present),
  neither half.

The three existing pins covering this key also pass:
`DetailSection.dueLikeReachesTheCell-9729`, `datetimeCell.dueLikeAffordance-8958`
and `DateCellRenderer` — 3 files, 21 tests, exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, filed as a finding for the seat (class c — a metadata trap).**
  The older `type: "detail"` block is a different schema with its own inline
  group-field entry, and its validator **accepts `dueLike` and silently strips
  it**. Measured with its control in the same run: `DetailSchema.safeParse` of a
  group field carrying the key returns success with the key **absent** from the
  parsed output, while `DetailViewFieldSchema.safeParse` of the byte-identical
  entry returns success with the key **kept**. That is the same
  accepted-parsed-dropped signature objectui#8958 recorded on the `datetime`
  cell. ⛔ Deliberately neither repaired nor written up here: under commandment #0.1 and
  ADR-0049 a declared-but-dropped key is enforced or removed, not written up,
  and that is a types/zod change, not this card's class.
- **Noted, ⛔ not filed.** `DetailViewField`'s own key set is documented nowhere
  in `content/docs`; the schema reference tabulates `DetailViewSchema`'s
  properties but no member table for the field entry. A missing member listing
  is incompleteness, not a defect, so it is not one of the three filing classes.
  Successor: whoever next extends that section.
- **No `Clause-②:` line is carried.** The card has no claim comment to copy one
  from (the comment listing for it returned an empty array, HTTP 200).
- ⛔ Left in draft, and no label written — the `domain:ui#2` seat lands this.
